description: A four-panel composite of MatCalc-simulated TTP (time–temperature–precipitation) diagrams for the investigated low-density Al–C steels. All panels share a logarithmic time axis (s, from 0.0001 to 1 000 000) and a linear temperature axis (200–1300 °C), drawn for a cooling rate of 100 Ks⁻¹. In each panel dotted/solid curves labelled 5%, 50% and 95% trace the precipitation progress of (Fe,M)ₓC_y, whose C-shaped nose sits near 900–1000 °C at ~10⁻³–10⁻² s. Horizontal dashed lines mark austempering temperatures (T_B) and end in star markers. Panel (a): header "T_A: 1150 °C", labels "T_B: 350 °C, Bt: 2300 s" and "T_B: 300 °C, Bt: 3600 s"; per the caption this is S1 and also approximately represents S2. Panel (b): header "T_A: 1220 °C", "T_B: 350 °C, Bt: 14000 s" and "T_B: 270 °C, Bt: 43000 s" (caption: S3) — curves shifted to far longer times. Panel (c) (caption: S4) is the only multi-system plot: header "T_A: 1250 °C, 1150 °C (900 s)", two grey shaded bands labelled TiMoC and (Fe,M)ₓC_y with 5%/95% boundaries, a vertical dashed reference line, and "T_B: 350 °C, Bt: 2600 s – 3000 s", "T_B: 320 °C, Bt: 3500 s". Panel (d) (caption: S5) has "T_A: 1150 °C", "T_B: 365 °C, Bt: 1000 s" and "T_B: 335 °C, Bt: 700 s", the shortest times. The group argues that (Fe,M)ₓC_y forms unavoidably during cooling, is retarded/suppressed only in S4 by the Ti–Mo–C system, and that S5 transforms fastest.

Caption assigns this panel to S1 (approximately representative of S2).

Caption assigns this panel to S4.

observations.observation: All four panels are TTP diagrams with Temperature (°C) on the y-axis (ticks 200–1300 in steps of 100) against Time (s) on a logarithmic x-axis (0.0001 to 1 000 000).
The header of every panel states a cooling rate of 100 Ks⁻¹.
Panels (a), (b) and (d) carry the boxed phase label (Fe,M)ₓC_y and three curves annotated 5%, 50% and 95%, showing a C-shaped nose at roughly 900–1000 °C at times of order 10⁻³–10⁻² s.
Panel (a) is labelled T_A: 1150 °C with austempering conditions 'T_B: 350 °C, Bt: 2300 s' and 'T_B: 300 °C, Bt: 3600 s' drawn as dashed lines ending in star markers.
Panel (b) is labelled T_A: 1220 °C with 'T_B: 350 °C, Bt: 14000 s' and 'T_B: 270 °C, Bt: 43000 s', i.e. much longer bainitic transformation times than panel (a).
Panel (d) is labelled T_A: 1150 °C with 'T_B: 365 °C, Bt: 1000 s' and 'T_B: 335 °C, Bt: 700 s', the shortest Bt values of the four panels.
Panel (c) is the only panel showing a second precipitate system: grey shaded bands labelled TiMoC and (Fe,M)ₓC_y, plotted for a double austenitisation 'T_A: 1250 °C, 1150 °C (900 s)'.
Panel (c) austempering labels read 'T_B: 350 °C, Bt: 2600 s - 3000 s' and 'T_B: 320 °C, Bt: 3500 s', and a vertical dashed reference line is drawn between the 100 and 10 000 s gridlines.
The caption assigns panel (a) to steel S1 and states that it is also approximately representative of steel S2, while (b), (c) and (d) correspond to S3, S4 and S5 respectively.

The citing text states that (Fe,M)ₓC_y particles precipitate during cooling due to extremely high nucleation kinetics between approximately 700 and 1150 °C in S1 and S3, and between 700 and 1000 °C in S5.

The citing text states that for S4 initial nucleation occurs rapidly between 700 and 950 °C but is subsequently suppressed by the counter-coarsening effect of the Ti–Mo–C precipitate system, with secondary precipitation requiring extremely long durations.
The citing text states that TTP curves indicate a slight increase in (Fe,M)ₓC_y in S3 compared with S1 and S2, attributed to higher Al content, with negligible impact on mechanical properties.

The citing text states that in S5 the moderate Al–C level and small Ni addition promote very rapid bainitic transformation when austempered slightly above Ms, consistent with the short Bt values printed in panel (d).
A short red mark (apparently a journal logo) sits at the lower-left of each panel near the origin of the time axis; its text is not legible.
